content.label:
Thanks for making the effort to build the simplest yet most powerful planning app I've seen so far, not to mention the elegance of the interface.
I've downloaded many similar apps in the last five years, but this one screams "use me" (in a good way).

I’ve always needed a Things app, I used to have the original things which is why I came back for it. I saw it was £10 and thought it was a bit too much for this type of app. However when you try all the free ones out there you’ll understand why this is £10. It just does everything right. 100% Recommend. 

The only thing I think could improve is the range of things you can do on your Apple Watch. I think you should be able to see further on rather than just today’s ‘To-Dos’.

I’m somewhat obsessed with this app. I’ve been battling for years to get organised, but nothing seemed to work. Things has changed all that - is simple enough not to be confusing, but adaptable enough to react to my various needs and has helped me to finally get on top of my wide and sprawling to-do lists and multiple projects. I downloaded it at the same time that I read Getting Things Done and they compliment each other extremely well. 

I wouldn’t be without it now, it basically helps me run my life and my business!

title.label: Nicely designed but dodgy watch sync

content.label:
Intuitive, easy to use and really well designed. 

My only issue so far has been syncing with my Apple Watch series 2. 

I have spent over an hour this morning debugging, resetting sync on both iPhone and watch and reinstalling both apps. 

Finally, the app has started syncing; I don’t know if this is the watch (seems ok on all other apps that sync) or the implementation?

The watch/iPhone sync functionality definitely needs to be made more robust in future releases.

title.label: Decent app, but not worth the money

content.label: Spent £10 on the iOS app. Was pretty happy with it until I realised the Mac App is an extra charge (and £50 at that!). Switched to a cheaper provider with same feature set.

title.label: The only organising app you'll ever need.

content.label:
Very comprehensive set of features, and it's very easy to add tasks and customise them.

Siri, calendar, reminders, and icloud integration is excellent.

I would really like a dark mode though.
Wasn’t sure but took the plunge & it was worth it.

This app has improved a lot over the years, this was one of my firs app I have ever bought in App Store back in 2008 with my first Apple ID, (this is a third time I buy it now). Cultured Code GmbH is still improving this app over the years so sensibly, it didn’t become unstable or overcomplicated. It offers lots of functionality under the simple and clean design! This app is a fantastic application I can highly recommend to anyone to get it, well worth it! Great job developers!
Things app is versatile to use, I use it for to do lists, wish lists organising and many more. This app makes my life a lot easier when I need to plan and organise.

title.label: A delightful app to use...would love more API features

content.label: I’ve tried a load of task management apps and they all tend to do better in one area or another. I had stuck with todoist for a long time but recently switch to things after the 3.0 redesign as I found the interface nicer and more pleasing to use AND I really valued the start date feature. However, I’d love to see some of todoists features like the ability to add tasks from other services which hook in. Still, great app.
I’ve used the app for serval years and the updates keep making it better and better. It syncs wonderfully with the iPhone and my iMac. The best and most used app I have. Thank you.

It’s the organisational app I’ve been looking for. I love how you can have projects and assign dates.
Development wise I’d love the ability to colour the stars differently as my husband and I share an apple account so have a shared ‘today’ list - having different coloured stars would help us to see quickly whose tasks are whose! Overall though, ACE!
Just installed this mainly due to the reviews and that it also ran on an iWatch. Well it doesn’t on mine. All I get is a splash screen for a couple of seconds then nothing

Uncomplicated, clean interface with plenty of functions. Much better than default ‘Reminders’ app on iPhone. Syncs nicely with my calendar to display events in the coming days and months. Love the ability to create tasks from other apps.

Frequent refreshes take many seconds to process (on latest phone and os). Gets really annoying especially when quick access needed. Also crashes if dragging multiple items to top after startup. Fix please. Price too high to have such basic flaws.

title.label: Good but drop off in new v3

content.label: Over all very good app which supports effective working. Would have given 4 or 5 stars except in latest version (v3) has made presentation difficult to see wood for greed. In v2 the areas were listed without the all the projects but in v3 the projects are listed as well. In v2 you could expend the areas to see the projects and there was a separate projects line that you could expand to see projects grouped by area. This I feel was better. Now, because of all the projects being listed I can’t do easily navigate and focus. I assume this is easily fixed. When it does I look forward to giving the app 5 stars. Ps. There are good additional features in v3 but not good enough to outweigh the negative step.
Apart from a new look it seems to be change for change’s sake and not a good value one too. It’s lucky for Things that Reminders is so useless, surprising too.
It's got a lovely interface. It is awkward to use. It's only a three for me as it doesn't have location alerts, which I use a lot travelling to various places.

I have used omnifocus for years and love it however things is so much quicker and I am starting the long slow focus of moving my tasks across from omnifocus. Especially since the new omnifocus came out this is so much more intuitive. If there were a way to quickly debunk everything from omnifocus to this I would be a very happy organised bunny

Nice app but extremely limited, no attachments, apple devices only, inflexible workflow, you can only get data in and not out (no export functionality). Very expensive, I've bought all the apps for other devices and find myself really regretting it.

I had more functionality with Wunderlist

It's overpriced if you want to get it on your phone and computer (has to be separate purchases for iPhone/iPad/mac). 

Generally the app is good, had zero issues and is quite pretty app for organising.

title.label: Great App - but not keen on the price across devices!!

content.label:
Would love to give this app 5 stars because it is that good - but when you consider what features are free with Wunderlist before you pay freemium prices... it's quite a lot. 

Would also be MUCH improved if you could share projects with other users.

I have used a lot of todo apps. I was initially put off if this app because of the cost. However due to its incredibly user friendly interface and syncing across all devices it's now become my most used app

title.label: Lovely but no PC or web interface!

content.label: Very nice, beautiful, easy to use etc. Will probably go back to MS tasks (boo) as not ability to see to-do's on my work PC. Means I have to have my iPad permanently open. Not awesome.

Amazing app and the new design improves Things SO much. However, why, when I add to dos (via Siri on my Apple Watch or iPhone) does Things have to put the in the inbox as 'From Reminders' and not straight into the inbox as to dos. I then have to go into Things to add them to the inbox proper. So untidy. I appreciate that this may be an Apple thing but really spoils a Magnificat that app.
Best app to organise your life and get stuff done!
I have to paid for "update" and the sinc  between my the old and new doesn't work. So I have data on old one and new one and paid £30 between iPhone and iPad. Sorry

Started with the free trial on Mac; didn't take me long to realise how valuable this incredibly simple yet intuitive and rich app can be personally and professionally. Bought it on all platforms now, though this works out as very expensive.

It really is excellent and is now being used everyday. It's expensive(£10) particularly given you need to pay extra for the iPad app. £10 pounds for one or £15 pounds for both would be more reasonable. (The iPad app is £20) It is at the end of the day just a to-do app albeit my favourite one.

Professional looking, easy to use and great functions such as projects, logbook & calendar importations. 

I would like in the future to see Alexa Support integrated into the app. "Alexa, What have I got to do today?"

I should have followed the advice: if it isn't broken don't fix it!
The new version is less clear and offers no advantage for the considerable fee across all the platforms.
Very disappointing from what had been one of my favourite apps.
I wish we could rely on Apple to deliver native Apps of this calibre, but until they catch up, this is a slick mo fo. Synched with the Mac version and my iWatch... it's a beautiful thing 😘
Since the last update I have no badge icon to notify me of tasks due today.. great app before the last change, love the new interface changes too, pls fix it soon..
I run my own business and use this everyday
The best productivity app I have downloaded to date. The aesthetics are high quality and the app is very intuitive.
I've used many todo apps but this is the best and it's so easy yet powerful that it actually gets used. Would thoroughly recommend.

Get-things-done reminder and to-do app. Several levels to it and allows you to start and monitor progress of projects or just simple things to be remembered. Really well thought through. Also the app talks to a lot of other productivity apps.

Paid £10 for this app for two reasons. On the surface it looked great and there was a lot of hype with it being recognised by Apple. My current GTD app of choice is 2Do which I think I paid £3 for. It may not be as pretty as Things but it's has far more customisable and is a lot more intuitive to use. Hopefully the team behind 2Do will add the only real feature that Things has over it and that is the drag and drop add feature and maybe a UI refresh. At £10 for an iPhone app it is vastly overpriced for its limited features I'm sorry to say. Hopefully you guys look at 2Do and make Things as powerful!

I love this app but it's a bit steep to get all three divides set up and for most it's to cost prohibitive. I accept you should pay for Mac version but not to have free sync between iPhone and iPad is the developers just being greedy and taking us for a ride. Comments from
Developers please!

This has a brilliant interface and it's so slick and user-friendly to interact with. However for ten quid I was really disappointed with the lack of configurability - no option to change the name of the core lists, can't even change the default font size! For the moment this is just far too locked down for me, Todo Cloud is still the much better option.
Just purchased.  So finding my way around.  I would like to email stuff to myself, after which I would then move to appropriate area.  Doesn't seem to do that... !!!

I'm happy to support app developers by buying apps. However, having spent nearly £60 upgrading to Things 3 on my Mac and iPhone, I think it's disingenuous to tell me that Things 2 on my iPad will no longer sync within Things Cloud, unless I spend another £20 on upgrading the iPad app. Presumably the wire format hasn't changed, so there's no technical reason for this limitation.

Things 3 has a sweet new UI and interaction model, but it's not necessarily more efficient. For example, you can no longer reschedule a to-do directly from the Today view in the iOS app; you have to move it to your Inbox first. EDIT: It turns out you can do this by swiping the to-do right, but it's not very discoverable.

The Logbook view needs some serious performance optimisation because scrolling through the thousands of to-dos I've accumulated during eight years is much slower than it was in Things 2. Finally, add in that the developers have ignored a simple question I have asked (twice) on Twitter and the financial investment begins to sting a bit.
Very simple to use and great design.
Very easy to use, better than other apps like Omnifocus , also cheaper 😉. Very sleek  looking. I love it !
Probably more features than I really need, but beautiful interface and designed with real care. Happy to pay for good apps.

I like many have spent time and money on task management apps, I tried the lot, this is a keeper, visually stunning, easy of use, more than worth the cost.
BIG THANKS AND CONGRATULATIONS
to the THINGS team

I got Things back in 2010 or thereabouts. Really liked it but found it slowly fell behind other apps. Switched to Todoist which had great functionality but I never quite enjoyed using as much a Things. 

Really pleased with Things 3. Took a long time coming but they wanted to get things just right (get it).
Simplicity concealing power

I've used things for years, have always found it an incredibly useful productivity tool, but this version is even better.  Really easy to maintain inbox zero, and to organise, prioritise & schedule tasks.

I'd started to worry Cultured Code had given up as Things had fallen so behind the curve - but the revamp is brilliant. The new sub-headings option, the Projects tucked under Areas and the Today window on your calendars all make this a one-stop planning resource and pleasure to use.
